After Kc2, Black still has Qa4+, another check. Kd2 is better because it creates a situation where Black's queen is trapped/undefended on a1, forcing Black into checks that all lose the queen.

**Best move:** Kd2

**Main line:** Kd2 Qxb2+ Qxb2 (White has won the queen)

**Motif:** attraction (the king move attracts/lures the queen to undefended squares where it can be captured)

**Coaching note (80 words):**
After Black's check Qa1+, you must move your king. But notice: on d2, your king not only escapes the check—it also attacks the queen on a1 via your rook on d1. Black's queen has no safe squares. Any checking move Black plays (Qxb2+, Qxd1+) allows you to recapture with your queen, winning a full piece. Look for moves that escape immediate threats while simultaneously trapping or attacking enemy pieces. That's how strong players spot tactics the first time.
